newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends steady on late support.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends steady on late support.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices ended steady on late support and a firmer cash market after easing in earlier sessions. Trading was slow as players awaited Nov 1-25 exports data and fresh export business next week. News that Thailand may export crude palm oil have no impact. Immediate support for Feb is 1,200.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Also firmed on refiners buying.
Prices are expected to hold above the 1,200 ringgit on expectation of fresh export business next week. "There was talk of an Egyptian tender next week," the dealer said.
At the close, February futures contract ended four ringgit up at 1,212 ringgit ($481.14) a tonne.
Morning prices had weakened because of lower soyoil futures in Chicago and lack of tenders from India and Pakistan.
Traders said news that Thailand may export crude palm oil did not have any impact on the market which fell in early trading on lower soyoil futures prices in Chicago.

"The Thai news has had no impact on the market. The amount of crude palm oil to be exported is not known yet," another trader said. "If Thailand exports, it won't sell a large quantity like Indonesia. Thailand will just export to its neighbouring countries while producers like Malaysia and Indonesia normally sell large quantities to other big buyers."

The Thai government may export crude palm oil to get rid of excess stocks estimated at 112,995 tonnes, a 117 percent rise from the same period last year, a commerce ministry source in Thailand said on Friday.
Trading was widespread but thin as big participation was absent. Turnover fell to 970 lots from 1,976 Thursday.
Some switching activities were seen from December to Frebruary and cross-trading, they said.
Among physical, Nov (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,215 ringgit with bids at 1,210 after trading from 1,202.50 and 1,215 and Nov (central) at 1,205 against 1,202.50.
Dec (south) saw offers at 1,230 ringgit and bids at 1,225 and earlier trades were 1,215 to 1,225, and Dec (central) was at 1,212.50 against 1,207.50.
Among refined products, Dec RBD palm oil was offered at $520 a tonne FOB Malaysia, and Jan/Feb/March at $517.50. Dec was traded at $515.
Dec RBD palm olein saw offers at $557.50 and Jan/Feb/Mar at $552.50. Dec was traded at $555 and Jan/Feb.Mar at $547.50.
Dec RBD palm stearin was offered at $377.50 and Dec/Jan palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $307.50. -- Tan Lee Lee (603-230-7510) ($1=2.5190 ringgit)
